analyst_view.overall: Early view: leaders Almería (29 pts, 24 scored, 10 conceded) host 21st-placed Albacete. Almería under Xavier García Pimienta were unbeaten in nine before the November round, while Albacete have revived under Joseba Etxeberria, who replaced Alberto González in October and has won three in a row, the last 3-1 at Leganés. The yellow-card ban listed for Marcos Luna should be served long before 13 December.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals. I lean a little lower: Almería have conceded only 10 in 13 and Albacete under Etxeberria have looked tighter, so I see Almería winning without a goal rush.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners. Almería should have most of the ball against a side fighting relegation, which fits that figure, and nothing in the news points either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards. Albacete are in a relegation fight and José Corpas picked up a three-match ban in October for a kick on an opponent, a sign of an edgy side, but the referee is not known yet, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.5 shots. Albacete gave up 17 shots at Leganés while still winning, and Almería at home will shoot a lot, so I see no reason to move away from a high total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target. Almería's attack is the best in the table and Albacete have scored on the break lately, so I stay close to the number.
